note.title: Aeneas and Creusa
note.overview: Aeneas and his family hurry through Troy to the fields. When they stop, he looks back and cannot see Creusa. He returns to search the streets and houses.
learningGoals: Recall the taught forms and facts independently.
Apply them to translation and GCSE-style questions.
Use the answer and individual mark points to improve precision.
summary: Aeneas and his family hurry through Troy to the fields. When they stop, he looks back and cannot see Creusa. He returns to search the streets and houses.
The woman he sees is Creusa’s ghost. The gods order her to stay and protect her. Aeneas must find a homeland for the Trojans.
He tries three times to grasp the ghost; each time it vanishes. His tears show grief; his return into danger supports an inference of devotion. Give an inference and specific linked evidence.

quickCheck.question: Line 1: Where were Aeneas and his family running?
quickCheck.stimulus:
Aeneas and Creusa · classroom extracts

1. Aeneas et familia per vias Troiae currebant. periculum timebant sed ad portam advenerunt et in agros festinaverunt.
2. ibi stiterunt. Aeneas respexit. Creusam non vidit. sed Creusam invenire non poterat.
3. Troiam iterum cucurrit. per portam festinavit, per vias villasque Creusam quaesivit.
4. feminam vidit. “discedere nunc debemus! Graeci Troiam habent. manere non possumus!”
5. sed femina non erat Creusa: umbra Creusae erat.
6. umbra, “dei” inquit “me manere iubent. Graeci me non habent; dei me custodiunt. sed iubent Aenean patriam Troianis invenire. nunc vale!”
7. ter Aeneas umbram comprendit; ter umbra evanuit. Aeneas lacrimabat.
8. Graecos nunc audivit. ad portam festinavit Troiaque discessit. ad familiam amicosque cucurrit.

Vocabulary: stiterunt = stopped; respexit = looked back; quaesivit = searched for; umbra = ghost; inquit = said; Aenean = Aeneas (accusative); Troianis = for the Trojans; vale = goodbye; ter = three times; comprendit = grasped / tried to grasp; evanuit = vanished; audivit = heard; discessit = left
